The National University of Kongju (Chungcheongnam-do, Gongju, Korea) produced the prealloyed powders by gas atomizing (N 2) with the Co-9Al-9W (at.%) composition.

The low energy milling (LEM) process was performed for 10 h at 150 rpm under Ar atmosphere, using 10 mm stainless steel balls and 80 mL stainless steel vials with a ball to powder ratio of 1.8:1 (Table 1).

other.foil: W foil to prevent C diffusion

evidence.quote: milled powder was consolidated by a fast-sintering technique, in this case by spark plasma sintering (SPS), which is a field assisted sintering technique, using an HPD-25 equipment (FCT System GmbH, Germany) at Nanomaterials and Nanotechnology Research Center (“Centro de Investigación en Nanomateriales y Nanotecnología”—CINN, Asturias, Spain). Discs of approximately 20 mm diameter and 5 mm thickness were produced, with a heating rate of 100◦C/min and a dwell of 5 min at 1200 ◦C, under 80 MPa of pressure.

evidence.quote: milled powder was consolidated by a fast-sintering technique, in this case by spark plasma sintering (SPS), which is a field assisted sintering technique, using an HPD-25 equipment (FCT System GmbH, Germany) at Nanomaterials and Nanotechnology Research Center (“Centro de Investigación en Nanomateriales y Nanotecnología”—CINN, Asturias, Spain). Discs of approximately 20 mm diameter and 5 mm thickness were produced, with a heating rate of 100◦C/min and a dwell of 5 min at 1200 ◦C, under 80 MPa of pressure.
First, a homogenization treatment was performed at 1250 ◦C for 24 h, followed by an ageing annealing treatment at 900 ◦C for 24 h. Heating and cooling rates were fixed at 5 ◦C/min.

Atomized and harmonic powders display a single phase, γ-fcc.
two small peaks at 41◦ and 43◦ can be depicted, which could belong to some hcp clusters that were formed after the low energy milling process.

After the first stage, as-sintered γ’ precipitates were already present without any subsequent heat treatment. These precipitates display a small size (24 nm approx. in average) but a high-volume fraction (75%).
Table 4 collects the size and volume fraction of the γ’ precipitates for each consolidation stage.
Following the homogenization treatment, the γ’ precipitates in the Co-9-9 At samples grew four times, on average, from 28 to 106 nm in size, taking on a cuboidal form.
Table 4 collects the size and volume fraction of the γ’ precipitates for each consolidation stage.

eventually, ageing heat treatment caused the γ’ precipitates to orient in accordance with the original γ grain, resulting in a larger more cuboidal γ’ precipitate (about 150 nm in size, see Figure 4), along with a decrease in volume fraction of these primary γ’ cuboids.

the γ’ precipitates in the Co-9-9-At-Harmonic material have grown due to the ageing treatment. However, because of the high energy that was retained in the lattice during the LEM process, the growth multiplied eight times its initial size (refer to Table 4).
Pure Co powders were added to Table 2 for comparison.
A harmonic structure is composed of a core of larger grain sizes surrounded by a connected shell of smaller grain sizes.

evidence.quote: The grain size of the powder after LEM is smaller in the edge than in the center of the powder particle (Figure 1d).
It is noticeable how the γ’ precipitates display different density and orientation in the regions divided by twin planes.

The deformed particles show an increase in the concentration of lattice defects that distort the order and lattice of the unit cell.

It is demonstrated that γ-γ’ Co-based superalloys could surpass the yield stress of Ni-based superalloys at high temperature due to the γ-γ’ structure.

in which the core grains cause an increase in strain and the shell grains cause an increase in stress, has also associated an improvement in the mechanical properties with the best balance between strength and toughness
